components: Cache-aside: requests or updates an item

steps: The application checks the cache for K.
A miss leaves the source of truth authoritative.
The application reads v3 from the database.
It fills v3 with a TTL, then returns it; writes invalidate or version this entry.

lesson.scenario: A product API loads a missing catalog record from the database and explicitly fills Redis.

steps.title: Cold cache
steps.narration: The database has product version 7 while Redis has no entry.
steps.outcome: The cache is treated as a disposable copy.
steps.invariant: The database remains the source of truth.

steps.title: Cache lookup misses
steps.narration: The API checks Redis before querying the database.
steps.outcome: The miss transfers refill responsibility to the API.
steps.invariant: A cache miss must not be interpreted as missing source data.

steps.title: Source read
steps.narration: The API reads authoritative version 7 from the catalog database.
steps.outcome: The API now has the response and cache payload.
steps.invariant: Refill data should carry a version or freshness boundary.

steps.title: Cache filled
steps.narration: The API stores version 7 with a five-minute TTL.
steps.outcome: Subsequent requests can avoid the database.
steps.invariant: Cache fill failure must not turn a successful source read into false data.

steps.title: Warm hit
steps.narration: A later request reads version 7 directly from Redis.
steps.outcome: The second request is served with lower source load.
steps.invariant: Write paths must invalidate or refresh the cached copy to bound staleness.
